title: PFOS exposure and periodontitis from adolescent burden to genetic and multiomics evidence.
byline: Wan H, Wang Z, Peng H, et al.
html: Periodontitis can develop early in life and may be influenced by persistent environmental exposures. We integrated Global Burden of Disease 2021 data, Mendelian randomization, transcriptomics, machine learning, immune profiling, single-cell analysis, molecular modeling, and in vitro validation to investigate links between perfluorooctane sulfonate exposure and periodontitis. Periodontal disease burden remained substantial among individuals aged 5-20 years and varied across sociodemographic strata. Genetically predicted PFOS exposure was associated with increased periodontitis risk by inverse-variance weighted Mendelian randomization. Multi-omics analyses identified 151 shared targets enriched in immune-inflammatory pathways and prioritized a ten-gene signature with strong diagnostic discrimination. Single-cell analysis implicated migration inhibitory factor (MIF)-centered immune communication, whereas molecular modeling supported stable PFOS-STK17B interactions. PFOS exposure in human gingival fibroblasts increased expression of the ten prioritized genes. These findings connect population burden with genetic, molecular, and experimental evidence supporting immune-inflammatory mechanisms linking PFOS exposure to periodontitis.
